evidence.description: Contract claims all REQ-AUTH-001 through REQ-AUTH-015 are covered, but REQ-AUTH-015 has no PROP and no test
PROP-AUTH-022 tests OAuth state instead of link session (mislabeled), PROP-AUTH-020 tests wrong function for env var validation
At least 6 integration tests (PROP-AUTH-012, 013, 014, 016, 024) are tautological — they construct literal expected values and assert against those literals, exercising zero implementation code
isSameOrigin uses string equality instead of RFC 6454 normalized comparison (case-insensitive host, default port awareness) as required by REQ-AUTH-008
maskSensitiveLogFields only masks top-level keys, not nested objects
Pure core correctly avoids I/O — createHash is deterministic. Reviewed lines 1-156.
Shell contains all side effects (crypto.randomBytes, Map I/O, console.log). Reviewed lines 1-102.
PROP-AUTH-010 concurrency test relies on single-threaded execution semantics, not actual atomicity mechanisms
Contract grading dimensions do not match VCSDD standard dimensions — Phase 3 adversary cannot evaluate against contract criteria
Tier 2 PROP count claims 17 but table has 16 entries

summary: Contract FAIL on all 5 dimensions. 5 critical findings: integration tests for PROP-AUTH-012/013/014/016/024 are tautological (assert hardcoded literals, not implementation output). 5 major findings: PROP-AUTH-022 tests wrong subsystem (OAuth state instead of link session), PROP-AUTH-020 tests wrong function for env var validation, REQ-AUTH-015 has no PROP or test, isSameOrigin lacks RFC 6454 normalization per REQ-AUTH-008, contract grading dimensions mismatch VCSDD standard, Tier 2 PROP count off-by-one. The contract cannot serve as a reliable grading rubric for Phase 3 in its current form.
